reason: REAL, and it survives the strongest counter-argument available to it. I drove all four refusals at 1440x960 in both rooms (?v=paper and ?v=ink, state=owner-editing) and read the CDP accessibility tree, not just the DOM. The describedby relationship the refutation would rest on is genuinely there and genuinely working: Accessibility.getPartialAXTree on #b-edit-date returns role=textbox, name="WHEN", describedby=b-edit-when-hint, and after each refusal the node's accessible DESCRIPTION does update - "Type the day first. For example, 3 October 2026." (empty), "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026." (banana), "That day has gone. Pick one still ahead." (1 January 2020), "Nothing can sit after Saturday 3 October 2026. Still Saturday 8 August 2026." (1 January 2030), with invalid flipping false->true in every case. So the finding could have been killed on "the description already does the work" - except that a description is only spoken when the AT computes the node's name/description, which is on focus, and focus never moves: focusedOnField===true after Enter in all four cases, and the field already had focus before it. NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver do not re-speak an accessible description because its target's textContent changed under a still-focused field; that is exactly why every form-validation pattern pairs aria-invalid with role=alert / a live region or moves focus. aria-invalid alone does not carry the refusal either - at absolute best a reader says "invalid entry", which names neither which rule was broken nor what to type, and no reader says even that reliably on an in-place attribute flip. There is no aria-errormessage on the field (null). I then proved the silence exhaustively rather than by absence-of-live-region: a MutationObserver over document.documentElement with subtree/childList/characterData/attributes recorded EXACTLY TWO mutations in the entire document across a refusal - aria-invalid on #b-edit-date and the childList write into #b-edit-when-hint - and NEITHER target is inside any [role=status], [role=alert], [role=log] or [aria-live] host (anyInLive: false). Byte-identical in the ink room. The contrast the seat draws is confirmed: on a valid date two live regions fire in the same instant - .b-undo becomes "Send the invitations moved 33 days later." and .b-stepRead (role=status) repaints "Thursday 10 September 2026 / in 56 days". So acceptance is announced twice and refusal is announced zero times, while the typed text stays in the field and the moment has silently not moved. The code reading is exact: p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint (render-b.js:1063) carries no role and no aria-live and is confirmed to be the element commitDate's root.querySelector(".b-ceiling") writes (it is the first .b-ceiling in the editor; the .b-standing sentence follows it). The in-product precedent is exact too: #b-empty-hint (render-b.js:1706 and 1788) is that field's aria-describedby target AND carries role="status" - identical construction, one attribute apart. And the standing gate assertion is correctly characterised: interaction-check.mjs:1193 tests /Nothing can sit after/ against document.querySelector(".b-ceiling").textContent, which proves the string was written and can never prove it reached a reader - the round-11 class again. Nothing in SETTLED.md covers this; entry 146/149 (one-move-two-announcements) is the accepted path, the opposite case. Not a restatement of any gate assertion, no constraint touched, no colour or weight involved.
sharpenedFix: Do not touch aria-describedby - the AX tree proves the description relationship and its update are already correct. The missing piece is only the announcement channel. In render-b.js:1063 change h("p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint", { text: "" }) to h("p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint", { role: "status", text: "" }), which is character-for-character the construction #b-empty-hint already ships. Prefer role="status" over aria-errormessage (thin AT support) and over role="alert" (assertive would cut across the .b-undo and .b-stepRead announcements on the accepted path, and would not match the precedent one screen away). The element is created empty when the editor opens and written only on a later user action, so the region is in the DOM well before its first change - no first-announcement race. The success path clears it to "", which announces nothing. Leave .b-ceiling.b-standing (render-b.js:1075) roleless: it never changes, and it sits second in document order so commitDate's querySelector(".b-ceiling") still resolves to the hint. Then harden the gate beside "the refusal says why" (interaction-check.mjs:1193): for BOTH rooms and for ALL FOUR refusals - empty, unreadable, a day that has gone, and over-ceiling - collect every [role=status], [aria-live] and [role=alert] on the page and require at least one to contain the refusal sentence, asserted against the live-region set rather than against .b-ceiling.textContent. Assert the same for #b-empty-hint's three refusals so the precedent is locked as well as copied.
